parameterNotes.dependency: the upstream that answered 503; the pricing service's error ratios are per dependency in the source, and this is the one that moved.
parameterNotes.answeredWith: the status the upstream answered with; the ratio series counts the responses, and a status code says which failure rather than how many.
parameterNotes.durationMinutes: how long the failures lasted, stated for a replay; the readings are shares and carry no duration of their own.

groundTruth.rootCauseReason: One upstream answered 503 on 60% of the pricing service's calls to it for eighteen minutes, while the pricing service's error rate against every other dependency stayed at zero and none of its own resources moved.

rootCauseIndicators.description: the dependency's own failure share, which is the same 60% the pricing service reports
zero against every other dependency, which is what localises the fault to one upstream

causalChain.mechanism: the tax service answered 503 to three calls in five for eighteen minutes, and the pricing service returned 502 for every call it could not complete

evidenceCheckpoints.description: the share of requests the pricing service refused with 502 for the eighteen minutes the upstream was degraded
the dependency's own failure share -- every failure the pricing service saw came from this call
the control: every other dependency answered correctly, so the fault is one upstream rather than the pricing service
the share the injection declared, which is the same number the telemetry reports -- two statements of one fact that now have to agree

remediation.action: fail over tax-calculation calls to the secondary provider while the upstream is degraded

query: The pricing service returned 502 on 60% of requests for eighteen minutes. Which component is the root cause, and what distinguishes it from the pricing service itself?
